title: U.S. House · Colorado's 3rd District
area: Western Slope and southern Colorado, including Grand Junction, Durango and Pueblo.

context.text: Incumbent Jeff Hurd defeated Ron Hanks in the Republican primary. Dwayne Romero defeated Alex Kelloff 54.8%-45.2% in the Democratic primary. This district was a closely watched swing seat in the 2024 election.

candidates.name: Jeff Hurd

summary.text: Jeff Hurd is the Republican incumbent for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A Grand Junction native and attorney, he practiced law in New York and western Colorado before entering Congress and sits on the Natural Resources, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology committees. He won renomination in the June 30, 2026 Republican primary.

background.text: Born in Grand Junction, Colorado, in 1979; according to his official biography, he grew up there and his first job was bagging groceries at a local store.
Earned a bachelor's degree in liberal studies from the University of Notre Dame, a J.D. from the University of Denver Sturm College of Law (2008), and an LL.M. from Columbia Law School (2010).
Worked at the Grand Junction Area Chamber of Commerce and clerked for 10th Circuit Judge Timothy Tymkovich.

According to his official biography, practiced law at Sullivan & Cromwell in New York City before returning to western Colorado, where he built a law practice focused primarily on rural electric cooperatives; Ballotpedia lists him as co-owner of a law firm.
Won the November 2024 general election with 50.8% of the vote over Democrat Adam Frisch (45.8%), succeeding Lauren Boebert.

Took office January 3, 2025. Committee assignments for 2025-2026 are Natural Resources (including chair of the Indian and Insular Affairs Subcommittee), Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology.
Defeated Ron Hanks in the June 30, 2026 Republican primary, 66.4% to 33.6%.
His official biography states that he lives in Grand Junction with his wife, Barbora, and their five children.

priorities.text: Lowering household energy costs, opposing state and federal regulations he says push families toward more expensive heating and electricity options.
Co-led a bipartisan framework (the HOPE Act / "CommonGround 2025") to temporarily extend enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits with new income caps and anti-fraud safeguards.

positions.summary: Criticized state and federal climate-driven regulations that push households and utilities away from natural gas toward electric heat pumps and other mandates, calling the added costs a "hidden tax" on families.
positions.quote: I’m fighting those in Congress for the same reason I’m fighting this one: working families should not have to bankroll regulatory experiments. Energy policy should start with common sense, not mandates.

positions.summary: Co-led the bipartisan HOPE Act to extend enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits for two years, with new income caps and anti-fraud provisions, to prevent a spike in health-insurance premiums.
positions.quote: The HOPE Act is a practical, bipartisan solution that maintains affordability, enhances transparency, and improves accountability while Congress works toward long-term reforms that will make our health-care system more stable and more affordable.

positions.summary: Told CPR News he is concerned that broad tariffs increase costs for consumers and that tariffs should be used with caution; the report notes he voted against President Trump's tariffs.
positions.quote: because those costs can get passed directly to Colorado consumers, to farmers and to businesses

record.text: Chairs the House Natural Resources Committee's Indian and Insular Affairs Subcommittee and serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Dwayne Romero is the Democratic nominee for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District. A West Point graduate and Army combat veteran, he served in Colorado Gov. John Hickenlooper's administration as Director of Economic Development, held several local offices in the Roaring Fork Valley area, and owns a property management company. He describes his campaign as centered on affordability, health care and government accountability.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was raised by a single mother and began working at age 12 folding laundry at his family's apartment complex.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1987, where his campaign says he was recruited to play baseball, and a graduate degree from Harvard Business School in 1997.

Served in the U.S. Army from 1984 to 1994 per Ballotpedia; his campaign says he served seven years in the Army Corps of Engineers, graduated from Ranger School, and earned a Bronze Star as a Combat Engineer Executive Officer during the Persian Gulf War, with a posting at Fort Carson, Colorado.
Served in then-Gov. John Hickenlooper's administration as Colorado's Director of Economic Development.

According to his campaign, held local offices including city council member, board member of his Fire Protection District and the Roaring Fork Transit Authority, and school district board member, serving as board president from 2020 to 2021.

Currently serves as an elected board director of the Snowmass Village Water and Sanitation District, according to his campaign website; also coached the local high school baseball team for nine years.
Owns and operates a property management company on the Western Slope that his campaign says employs 120 people.
According to his campaign, lives with his wife, Margaret, a longtime kindergarten teacher, and they have three daughters; his campaign address is in Woody Creek.

priorities.text: Lowering cost of living: proposes repealing tariffs he says are raising fuel and grocery prices, and expanding the Family Tax Credit.
Protecting Colorado's water resources amid Colorado River Compact challenges and drought.
Supporting family farms and ranches with a robust Farm Bill and restrictions on foreign ownership of Colorado water and farmland.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to repeal what he calls 'disastrous tariffs' that are raising the cost of living for the district.
Describes an 'all-of-the-above' energy approach that uses the district's existing energy resources while also advancing alternative energy deployment.
Calls for building more housing, repealing what he describes as outdated construction red tape, and stopping large investors from buying up homes to drive up rents.
Told CPR News he would work to repeal parts of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, including its cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.

candidates.name: Cory Robertson

summary.text: Cory Robertson is the Libertarian Party nominee for U.S. House in Colorado's 3rd District. The Libertarian Party of Colorado lists him as its candidate for the district; little other biographical information is publicly available.

background.text: Listed by the Libertarian Party of Colorado as its 2026 candidate for Congressional District 3.
Appears on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for U.S. House Colorado District 3, per Ballotpedia.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, public statements, or completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey found (Ballotpedia page checked Oct. 19, 2026; iVoterGuide profile has no platform text).

candidates.name: Clifton Brown

summary.text: Clifton Brown is an unaffiliated candidate for U.S. House in Colorado's 3rd District. Ballotpedia lists his profession as carpenter. In a Ballotpedia survey he says he will accept no corporate or PAC money and favors ending congressional districts.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Cherry Creek High School, per Ballotpedia.
Career experience includes working as a carpenter, per Ballotpedia.
In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he states that he will not accept money from any corporation or PAC and will not earn more than his government salary.

priorities.text: Pledges not to take money from any corporation or PAC and not to earn more than the government salary.
Says gerrymandering should stop and calls for ending congressional districts.
Calls for a "citizen protection act" limiting voting, campaign contributions and real estate ownership to citizens.

candidates.researchNotes: Unaffiliated. Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey (2026); his survey mentions the site ruhero.com, which was not fetched. His answers do not directly take a side on most listed issues.

statements.quote: I believe that saving the planet is our biggest responsibility as Americans.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey
